summary: Websurfx is an open-source metasearch engine written in Rust that queries multiple upstream search providers simultaneously. It strips out advertisements and telemetry to return aggregated results with a focus on user privacy. It serves as a direct alternative to platforms like SearX.
goodFor: It suits self-hosters who want to bypass commercial search engine tracking and advertising while maintaining a lightweight infrastructure.
watchOut: The project overlaps heavily with the more mature and widely adopted SearXNG, and upstream changes to target search engines can occasionally break result parsing.
deployNotes: As a containerised Rust application, you will typically deploy it via Docker behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination, with minimal persistent storage requirements as it generally does not rely on a separate database.
